【原视频简介】
Restoration of Antique Bowie Knife — It Took 335 Hours! Hi! Today, restoration of a rare antique 19th-century Bowie knife. This is a unique piece. Of course, the knife is in poor condition. The original handle is missing, and the one currently on it was most likely installed sometime in the 20th century. There is a lot of rust, and the sheath is missing. But now I’m going to fix all of that. I bought this piece at a flea market.

00:00 Start
01:14 Blade Cleaning
04:05 Knife Sanding
06:52 Making Blade Collar
12:55 Making Knife Guard
15:37 Knife Handle
23:06 Handle Sanding
25:08 Making Pommel
26:47 Engraving the Pommel
32:16 Leather Knife Sheath
42:42 Before and After
43:37 Test

First, I removed the old handle and discovered that the tang was broken. On top of that, it was very short for a knife of this size. I removed the surface rust, filled the knife with kerosene, and left it for two days. After two days, I took it out of the kerosene, wiped it down, applied WD-40, and then used heated machine oil. I thoroughly coated the entire knife, wrapped it in a cloth and a plastic bag, and left it for another three days. 

After three days, all of the remaining rust came off very easily. Then I did some light hand sanding. I also used polishing paste, but all of the history remained on the blade. I deliberately left the nicks on the blade because they are minor, and removing them would have meant changing the geometry of the blade and, therefore, changing its history. I don’t like doing that.
